marble.name: Narrative Writing
marble.subject: English
marble.description: Write narratives with developed settings, characters and plot, using dialogue and description to develop experiences and show character responses to situations
marble.prompt: When you writes a story, do they bring it to life with descriptions of the setting, details about the characters, and some dialogue — rather than just listing what happened?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning to write their own stories and explanations — planning what to say, putting events in order, and sharing their writing with others for feedback.

authoredAnswer: Writes a narrative with a described setting, a character with a problem, dialogue revealing feelings or personality and a resolution, and explains the dialogue’s role.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Writes a chain of events (“He went… then he found… then he went home”) with no sentence describing where it happens and no speech or reaction showing what the character is like. Evidence basis: Common Core State Standard
wrongAnswers.fix: Mark the first event and ask “Where is the character and what can they see or hear?”; the child adds one setting sentence there and one line of dialogue at the problem showing how the character feels.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: The ending removes the problem with no action by a character (“Then the storm stopped and everything was fine”) or solves a different problem from the one set up. Evidence basis: Graham et al. (2012, rev. 2018), Teaching
wrongAnswers.fix: Write the problem at the peak of the story mountain and ask “What does your character do to fix this?”; the child writes that action in the resolution box and rewrites the ending to follow from it.
